device.name: Matter Device (Matter-over-Wi-Fi / Thread node)
device.notes:
Matter is the cross-ecosystem smart-home standard (from the Connectivity Standards Alliance) that runs over Wi-Fi/Ethernet and Thread. A Matter device advertises itself over mDNS/DNS-SD with two standard, vendor-neutral service types:
  _matter._tcp   — an OPERATIONAL node: already commissioned onto at least
                   one fabric. The instance name is
                   <compressed-fabric-id>-<node-id> in hex (not
                   human-friendly). TXT keys are timing hints: SII/SAI/SAT
                   (idle/active/sleep intervals), T (TCP support).
  _matterc._udp  — a COMMISSIONABLE node: advertising that it is ready to be
                   added. Richer TXT: D (discriminator), VP ("vid+pid"),
                   CM (commissioning mode), DT (device type), DN (a friendly
                   device name), PH/PI (pairing hints). Also carried as the
                   _L<longdiscriminator> / _S<shortdiscriminator> and
                   _CM subtypes.
A Thread-only Matter device is reached through a Thread Border Router and is not directly on the IP segment; the ones this spec sees are the Matter-over-Wi-Fi/Ethernet nodes (and border routers, which are on Wi-Fi).
This project does NOT commission or drive Matter devices: commissioning needs the device's setup passcode (the 11-digit code / QR) and would enroll this app as a fabric admin, and ongoing control speaks the Matter operational protocol — both out of scope. We DISCOVER the node, draw a generic smart-device pictogram (Matter spans plugs, bulbs, sensors, locks and more, and the operational advertisement does not name the type), and leave control to whatever Matter controller the user already runs. There is no local web admin UI, so no admin_url is offered.
Display name: a commissionable node's TXT DN is human-friendly; an operational node has only its hex instance name, so the mDNS instance name is the display fallback. Stable key: the operational instance name (fabric+ node id) or the hostname.

credentials.notes: Identify-only: no credential crosses to this app. The Matter setup passcode is entered by the user in their Matter controller during commissioning, never here.

factory_reset.description:
There is no single gesture to transcribe, and that is a property of Matter rather than a gap here: the specification says what a reset must ACHIEVE and leaves how the user triggers it to the manufacturer, so the button, hold time and indicator come from the individual product's manual. What a reader gains from this entry is the guarantee about the outcome, which is the same on every certified device: after a reset the node is commissionable again, and nothing of the previous owner's fabric survives on it.
Removing the device from every fabric through a controller achieves the same removal of operational identity without touching the hardware, and is the route to prefer when the device is still reachable.
factory_reset.effect: The Matter specification is unusually precise about this, which is the advantage of a device that implements a published standard: a factory reset SHALL remove from the node all security- and privacy-related data and key material created during or after commissioning, except what is explicitly required to persist across resets. Operational node identifiers go with it, as they do when a fabric is removed. It clears nothing this spec's consumers store — this entry only identifies the device.

procedures.basis: Matter 1.0 core specification, section 13.4 Factory Reset, which mandates the outcome but leaves the trigger to the manufacturer. The specific gesture must come from the product's own documentation.
procedures.name: The manufacturer's own decommission gesture

steps.action: Perform the decommission or factory-reset gesture documented for the specific product.
steps.expect: The node returns to a commissionable state with all commissioning-derived key material removed.

methods.description: No provisioning is performed here. The device is commissioned onto a Matter fabric with its setup passcode via a Matter controller (Apple Home, Google Home, SmartThings, Alexa, Home Assistant), after which it is discovered passively by its _matter._tcp advertisement.

setup.notes: Nothing for this app to provision: a Matter node advertises itself over mDNS. We browse the standard service types, draw the pictogram and leave commissioning/control to the user's Matter controller. Confidence high: the service types and TXT keys are the CSA standard's, and an operational node was seen live.

rejoin.notes: The node stays discoverable by its DNS-SD advertisement wherever it sits on the LAN; identity keys on the operational instance name (fabric+node id) or hostname, not IP.

testing.notes: Matter discovery verified live 2026-08-16: a real commissioned node advertised the operational DNS-SD service _matter._tcp over mDNS on the segment, decoded by the standard service types below. Identify-only: this project does not join the Matter fabric (commissioning requires the device's setup passcode and puts the app on the device's fabric — out of scope), so it recognises the device, shows a pictogram, and leaves control to the user's existing Matter controller (Home/SmartThings/Alexa/Google).

local_access.summary: Matter is a local-first, cross-vendor standard with no required cloud — fully locally controllable through any Matter controller. This project deliberately scopes the entry to identify-only and defers control to the controller the user already runs.
